items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the insurance law, in relation to requiring certain health
insurance policies include coverage services provided by pharmacists related
to contraceptives
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S6441

SPONSOR: SKOUFIS
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the insurance law, in relation to requiring certain
health insurance policies include coverage services provided by pharma-
cists related to contraceptives

 
PURPOSE:

This legislation will increase the number of pharmacists offering
contraception pursuant to a non-patient specific standing order by
providing reimbursement for their services.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1: Amends clause (v) of subparagraph (E) of paragraph 17 of
subsection (i) of section 3216 of the insurance law, to mandate coverage
for all FDA-approved contraceptive drugs, devices, and procedures,
including over-the-counter options, voluntary sterilization, and related
patient education, counseling, and follow-up services. Coverage must not
impose restrictions or delays, and at least one therapeutic or pharma-
ceutical equivalent must be provided without cost-sharing. Emergency
contraception must be covered without cost-sharing when prescribed or
lawfully obtained over-the-counter. If a healthcare provider determines
a non-covered contraceptive is necessary, their decision is final, and
an exception process must be available. Coverage shall include
reimbursement to a pharmacist who prescribes and dispenses contraceptive
drugs, devices, and other products and services like any other health
care provider.

Section 2: Amends subparagraph (A) of paragraph 16 of subsection (1) of
section 3221 of the insurance law, to require that all group or blanket
health policies must cover FDA-approved contraceptive drugs, devices,
and procedures, including over-the-counter options, voluntary steriliza-
tion, patient education, and follow-up services.  Coverage must include
at least one therapeutic or pharmaceutical equivalent without cost-shar-
ing, with exceptions if medically necessary. Emergency contraception
must be covered without cost-sharing when prescribed or lawfully
obtained over-the-counter.  Policies must allow up to a 12-month supply
of contraceptives at once and reimburse pharmacists for prescribing and
dispensing contraceptives like other healthcare providers.

Section 3: The opening paragraph and subparagraph (A) of paragraph 1 of
subsection (cc) of section 4303 of the insurance law, all medical and
major medical insurance contracts must cover FDA-approved contraceptive
drugs, devices, and procedures, including over-the-counter options, with
at least one therapeutic or pharmaceutical equivalent provided without
cost-sharing. If the available versions are medically inadvisable, an
alternate must be covered at no cost. A healthcare provider's determi-
nation of the need for a non-covered contraceptive is final, with an
exception process in place. Coverage must also include emergency contra-
ception without cost-sharing, allow up to a 12-month supply of contra-
ceptives at once, and ensure pharmacists are reimbursed for prescribing
and dispensing contraceptives like other healthcare providers.

Section 4: Sets Effective Date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

This bill would allow pharmacists to bill state-mandated private insur-
ance providers for their time spent prescribing contraception.  This
measure is essential to increasing pharmacist participation in providing
contraceptive services while eliminating out-of-pocket costs for
patients.

As New York anticipates a 27% shortage of primary care physicians over
the next decade, the role of pharmacists in the healthcare system will
become increasingly vital. With the pharmacist workforce expected to
grow, these professionals will be well-positioned to help address the
state's healthcare needs. By ensuring reimbursement for their services,
this bill will alleviate pressure on primary care providers and improve
access to contraception, particularly in underserved and rural communi-
ties.

Pharmacists are among the most accessible healthcare professionals,
offering convenient locations, extended hours, and services without the
need for appointments. These advantages make them a crucial resource
compared to the limitations of traditional primary care settings. Howev-
er, without appropriate reimbursement for their time and expertise in
prescribing contraception, many pharmacists may be discouraged from
fully embracing this expanded role. By addressing this barrier, the bill
will enhance healthcare accessibility and strengthen contraceptive care
throughout New York.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New Bill

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately and shall apply to policies and
contracts issued, renewed, modified, altered or amended on and after
such date.

BILL NUMBER: S6441A

SPONSOR: SKOUFIS
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the insurance law, in relation to requiring certain
health insurance policies include coverage services provided by pharma-
cists related to contraceptives

 
PURPOSE::

This legislation will increase the number of pharmacists offering
contraception pursuant to a non-patient specific standing order by
providing reimbursement for their services.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS::

Section 1: Provides that individual health insurance coverage shall
include reimbursement to a pharmacist who dispenses self-administered
hormonal contraceptives pursuant to section 6801 of the Education Law
and provides related services the same as any other health care provid-
er.

Section 2: Provides that group health insurance coverage shall include
reimbursement to a pharmacist who dispenses self-administered hormonal
contraceptives pursuant to section 6801 of the education law and
provides related services the same as any other health care provider.

Section 3: Provides that Article 43 health insurance coverage shall
include reimbursement to a pharmacist who dispenses self-administered
hormonal contraceptives pursuant to section 6801 of the education law
and provides related services the same as any other health care provid-
er.

Section 4: Sets Effective Date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

ance providers for their time spent dispensing contraception.  This

items.memoText:
VETO MESSAGE - No. 50
 
TO THE SENATE:
 
I am returning herewith, without my approval, the following bill:
 
Senate Bill Number 6441-A, entitled:
 
    "AN ACT to amend the insurance law, in relation to requiring certain
      health  insurance  policies  include coverage services provided by
      pharmacists related to contraceptives"
 
    NOT APPROVED
 
  This bill would amend the Insurance Law  to  require  that  commercial
health insurance policies reimburse pharmacists dispensing self-adminis-
tered  hormonal  contraceptives and providing related services "the same
as any other health care provider."
 
  In 2023, I signed the Birth Control Access Act {"BCAA"), which author-
izes pharmacists to dispense self-administered  hormonal  contraceptives
pursuant  to a non-patient specific standing order from a physician. The
BCAA allowed New Yorkers to access safe and effective contraception from
their local pharmacy, and  pharmacists  across  the  State  are  already
utilizing  this  new authority. Commercial health insurance policies are
required to cover contraceptive drugs, devices, and products,  including
self-administered hormonal contraceptives dispensed by pharmacists, with
no cost-sharing to the insured. I was proud to sign this landmark legis-
lation,  as  reproductive  rights are under attack across the country, I
will continue to ensure that New York remains a safe harbor for those in
need of reproductive health care.
 
  While the bill would increase reimbursements for pharmacists  dispens-
ing  contraceptives,  it  would  require health insurers to update their
medical billing systems to comply, an administrative burden that carries
with it significant costs. Additionally, pharmacy benefit managers would
be able to charge health insurers for reimbursements paid to  a  pharma-
cist,  further  increasing  costs.  Such costs would likely be passed on
from the health insurers  to  employers  and  consumers  through  higher
premiums.
 
  Therefore, I am constrained to veto this bill.
 
  The bill is disapproved.                       (signed) KATHY HOCHUL
 
                               __________
